docs.title: Layout Implications
docs.text:
The chosen layout significantly impacts memory usage and query performance:

  • bidirectional_t (Default): Maintains two internal flattened lists (vertex-to-hyperedges and hyperedge-to-vertices). Provides optimal \(O(1)\) degree/size lookups and fast traversals in both directions at the cost of doubled memory consumption.
  • vertex_major_t: Maintains only a vertex-to-hyperedges flattened list. Highly memory efficient and fast for querying vertex degrees or incident hyperedge sets, but querying hyperedge sizes or incident vertex sets requires expensive full-graph scans.
  • hyperedge_major_t: Maintains only a hyperedge-to-vertices flattened list. Memory efficient and fast for hyperedge-centric queries, but querying vertex degrees or incident hyperedge sets requires full-graph scans.

  • LayoutTag Specifies the memory layout orientation for the underlying data structure.

docs.title: Layout Implications
docs.text:
The chosen layout significantly impacts memory usage and query performance:

  • bidirectional_t (Default): Maintains two internal lists (vertex-to-hyperedges and hyperedge-to-vertices). Provides optimal \(O(1)\) degree/size lookups and fast traversals in both directions at the cost of doubled memory consumption.
  • vertex_major_t: Maintains only a vertex-to-hyperedges list. Highly memory efficient and fast for querying vertex degrees or incident hyperedge sets, but querying hyperedge sizes or incident vertex setss requires expensive full-hypergraph scans.
  • hyperedge_major_t: Maintains only a hyperedge-to-vertices list. Memory efficient and fast for hyperedge-centric queries, but querying vertex degrees or incident hyperedge sets requires full-hypergraph scans.

Template parameters:

  • LayoutTag Specifies the memory layout orientation for the underlying data structure.
  • IdType The underlying integer type used for identifiers.

docs.text: This module houses a variety of general-purpose data structures and types. Though they are utilized natively by hypergraph implementations, these components are carefully decoupled from specific hypergraph logic, they can be seamlessly extracted and utilized in broader contexts.

docs.title: typedef default_id_type
docs.text:
The default unsigned integer type used for vertex and hyperedge identifiers. 

using hgl::default_id_type = typedef gl::default_id_type;

See also: gl::default_id_type

docs.title: typedef flat_jagged_vector
docs.text:
A flattened 2D vector (jagged array) providing efficient storage for variable-length segments. 

template<std::semiregular T>
using hgl::flat_jagged_vector = typedef gl::flat_jagged_vector<T>;

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: These utilities provide a curated set of general-purpose tools that support the library's internal algorithms and hypergraph modeling operations, completely independent of strict hypergraph theory semantics.

docs.text:

docs.text:
A view concatenating two ranges sequentially (C++20 polyfill for C++26 std::views::concat ).

using hgl::util::concat_view = typedef gl::util::concat_view<V1, V2>;

docs.title: See Also
docs.text: • gl::util::concat_view : For the full type definition.

docs.title: variable concat
docs.text:
Concatenates two viewable ranges into a concat_view . 

constexpr concat_fn hgl::util::concat = {};

docs.title: Example usage
docs.text:
std::vector<int> v1 = {1, 2, 3};
std::vector<int> v2 = {4, 5, 6};
auto concatenated = gl::util::concat(v1, v2);
for (int x : concatenated)
    std::cout << x << " "; // Output: 1 2 3 4 5 6

Parameters:

  • r1 First range to concatenate.
  • r2 Second range to concatenate.

Replace with std::views::concat (C++26).

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
This namespace pulls in practical, domain-agnostic C++ range utilities from gl::util. Because hypergraphs share the same underlying memory models and algorithmic requirements as standard graphs, they seamlessly reuse the same fundamental C++20 range utilities and helpers.

Note

To get a detailed overview of these shared utilities, please refer to the GL module's General Utilities documentation page.

Here is a list of all modules:

  • Graph Library (GL) The top-level module defining the general-purpose C++ template graph library.

    • Graph Algorithms Generic graph algorithms, foundational search templates, and related utilities.

    • Core Graph Components Fundamental graph data structures, element descriptors, and configuration tags.

    • I/O Utility I/O stream operations, formatting, and serialization of graph data.

    • Graph Topologies Generators and evaluators for standard structural graph topologies.

    • Traits & Concepts Type traits, template constraints, and compile-time metaprogramming utilities.

    • Generic Types Independent, high-performance data structures and utility types.

    • General Utilities Practical, domain-agnostic C++ helpers, mathematical functions, and polyfills.

  • Hypergraph Library (HGL) The top-level module defining the general-purpose C++ template hypergraph library.

    • Hypergraph Algorithms Generic hypergraph algorithms, search templates, and related utilities.

    • Core Hypergraph Components Fundamental hypergraph data structures, element descriptors, and configuration tags.

    • I/O Utility I/O stream operations, formatting, and serialization of hypergraph data.

    • Traits & Concepts Type traits, template constraints, and compile-time metaprogramming utilities.

    • Generic Types Independent, high-performance data structures and utility types.
